record.context_brief: Admissible walks with bounded even step sizes
record.original_question: For a fixed positive integer m, let F_m be the set of all nonzero even integers j with |j| <= m. A walk x from -n to n is a finite sequence of nonzero even steps x(t) whose total sum is 2n; writing the intermediate vertices as j(0) = -n and j(t) = -n + sum_{i=1}^t x(i), the walk is admissible when j(t) is never equal to ±n for 1 <= t <= ν, where ν + 1 is the number of steps. Let X_n^+(F_m) be the set of admissible walks from -n to n that use only positive steps from F_m, and for each such walk define h(x) = (∏_{t=1}^ν [n^2 - j(t)^2]^{-1})(∏_{t=1}^{ν+1} V(x(t))). For z = (V(2), V(4), ..., V(2m)) ∈ C^m, define P_{m,n}(z) = ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x). Determine these polynomials P_{m,n}(z), and/or determine their asymptotic behavior for fixed m as n → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer m and a positive integer n. Let F_m = { j ∈ 2ℤ \ {0} : |j| ≤ m } be the set of nonzero even integers of absolute value at most m.

A walk from −n to n is a finite sequence x = (x(1), x(2), …, x(ν+1)) of nonzero even integers (the "steps") whose sum equals 2n. Define the vertices of the walk by
  j(0) = −n,  j(t) = −n + Σ_{i=1}^{t} x(i)  for 1 ≤ t ≤ ν+1,
so that j(ν+1) = n. The walk is called admissible if j(t) ≠ ±n for every 1 ≤ t ≤ ν.

Let X_n^+(F_m) denote the set of admissible walks from −n to n in which every step x(t) lies in F_m and is positive (so x(t) ∈ {2, 4, …, m} when m is even, or x(t) ∈ {2, 4, …, m−1} when m is odd).

To each formal symbol V(2k) (k = 1, …, m/2 rounded down) associate a complex variable, and write z = (V(2), V(4), …, V(2⌊m/2⌋)) ∈ ℂ^{⌊m/2⌋}. For each walk x ∈ X_n^+(F_m) define the weight
  h(x) = ( Π_{t=1}^{ν} [n² − j(t)²]^{-1} ) · ( Π_{t=1}^{ν+1} V(x(t)) ).

Define the polynomial
  P_{m,n}(z) = Σ_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x).

Problem: Determine an explicit closed form for the polynomials P_{m,n}(z), and/or determine their asymptotic behavior as n → ∞ with m fixed.

artifact.status_search_result: A combinatorial identity of Djakov–Mityagin associated with the simplest two-term case (essentially m = 4) has been given a direct combinatorial proof (Zagier, and subsequent work). However, no published source found explicitly resolves the general problem of finding closed forms or asymptotics of P_{m,n}(z) for arbitrary m, so the general question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On a Combinatorial Identity of Djakov and Mityagin
status_evidence.snippet: Combinatorial proof given for a specific identity arising from Djakov–Mityagin's spectral asymptotics for two-term potentials.
status_evidence.claim: The case corresponding to a specific small m has been resolved combinatorially, but not the general family P_{m,n}.

status_evidence.title: Convergence of spectral decompositions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Djakov–Mityagin work on Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials motivating the walk sums.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the analytic context but does not provide closed forms or asymptotics for general P_{m,n}.
